top_news.title: KSE-Web: An Analysis of Hybrid Retrieval and LLM-Assisted Query Expansion for Low-Resource Khmer Semantic Search
top_news.dek: Researchers introduce KSE-Web, a framework for Khmer semantic search using hybrid retrieval and LLM-assisted query expansion.
top_news.brief: Khmer is a low-resource language with significant retrieval challenges, including ambiguous word boundaries and limited annotated data. KSE-Web addresses these by combining hybrid retrieval methods with LLM-based query expansion, tested on a curated dataset of 3,000 cleaned documents and 300 manually reviewed search queries.
top_news.image_alt: Diagram showing the KSE-Web retrieval pipeline for Khmer language processing.

top_news.title: Ukraine opens its massive labeled battlefield dataset to British firms in a landmark AI weapons partnership
top_news.dek: Ukraine is sharing its massive 'Universal Military Dataset' of combat imagery with British firms to accelerate military AI development.
top_news.brief: The UK has gained access to Avengers Labs, a platform containing five million annotated combat images and sensor data from the Ukrainian front line. The data, which includes drone and acoustic sensor feeds, is being used to train models for classifying military hardware like tanks and artillery.
top_news.image_alt: A drone view of a battlefield with AI-annotated bounding boxes on military equipment.

top_news.title: CUDA Python 1.0: Stable APIs, One Foundation, Full Platform Access
top_news.dek: NVIDIA has released CUDA Python 1.0, providing a stable, unified API for direct GPU access without requiring C++ extensions.
top_news.brief: CUDA Python 1.0 bridges the gap between high-level libraries like PyTorch and low-level CUDA C++. It allows developers to access the full GPU platform directly from Python, simplifying custom kernel development and improving interoperability between different GPU-accelerated libraries.
top_news.image_alt: NVIDIA CUDA Python 1.0 logo and architecture diagram

top_news.title: Qwen 3.8-Flash-Next releasing tomorrow (125B a6B)
top_news.dek: Alibaba's Qwen team is set to release Qwen 3.8-Flash-Next, a 125B parameter model.
top_news.brief: The upcoming Qwen 3.8-Flash-Next model features 125 billion parameters. It will be available via the ModelScope platform, continuing the series' focus on high-performance, large-scale language modeling.
top_news.image_alt: Qwen model logo on ModelScope platform

top_news.title: Introducing the Admin plugin for ChatGPT Work and Codex
top_news.dek: OpenAI launched an Admin plugin for ChatGPT Work and Codex to streamline workspace management via natural language.
top_news.brief: The new Admin plugin allows administrators to query workspace data, manage member permissions, and adjust settings directly through a conversational interface. This eliminates the need to navigate multiple dashboards or construct complex manual configurations.
top_news.image_alt: Admin plugin interface for ChatGPT Work

primary.title: CUDA Python 1.0: Stable APIs, One Foundation, Full Platform Access
primary.summary: For years, a Python developer who needed a GPU had two realistic choices: Learn NVIDIA CUDA C++ well enough to write an extension, set up a build toolchain, and... For years, a Python developer who needed a GPU had two realistic choices: Learn NVIDIA CUDA C++ well enough to write an extension, set up a build toolchain, and maintain bindings back to Python, which most people never did; or move up the stack and let someone else’s library do it, namely PyTorch, CuPy, or RAPIDS. The second option is why the Python GPU ecosystem thrives. But it has limits. Source
